title: Sticky US CPI and Gulf Energy Shut-Ins Firm Global Yields as India's Current Account Deficit Expands
changed: A 0.4% monthly US October CPI print slowed expected Federal Reserve rate cuts, pushing US Treasury yields and the dollar higher. In Europe, UK Q3 GDP growth of 0.7% reduced urgency for Bank of England monetary easing, keeping gilt yields firm. The Bank of Japan maintained its ultra-easy monetary stance without rate hikes this year, sustaining yen carry-trade flows into higher-yielding assets, though persistent Japanese wholesale inflation maintains eventual rate normalization risks.

Energy markets faced supply-side disruptions as Hurricane Isaias forced production shut-ins along the US Gulf Coast, maintaining upward pressure on Brent crude prices. In global technology, an espionage probe and Congressional summons involving Nvidia introduced governance risks across semiconductor supply chains, while Anthropic set a benchmark for AI capex by targeting a $1.3 trillion valuation range.

India's external balance faced pressure as the September current account deficit expanded to $7.4 billion, increasing domestic vulnerability to elevated crude import costs. In sovereign debt markets, institutional demand absorbed ₹34,000 crore of 10-year G-secs at a 7.3203% cut-off yield with a bid-to-cover ratio above 2x, supported by an RBI debt switch auction of ₹25,000 crore. Systemic liquidity showed signs of tightening, as banks parked under half the notified amount in a ₹75,000 crore VRRR auction before the RBI absorbed ₹38,592 crore at a 5.49% cut-off.

Indian equities saw the Nifty rebound to 25,358 on renewed foreign institutional buying. Fortnightly banking data showed persistent loan-to-deposit ratio pressure as deposit growth lagged credit demand, constraining net interest margins. Regulatory actions tightened non-bank credit access through the cancellation of Gandhinagar Leasing's registration and the one-year board supersession of Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank.

For your corporate tax and compliance practice, the RBI delegated FEMA compounding powers to regional offices, reducing processing timelines for cross-border trade lapses alongside updated FEMA export-import documentation rules. Financial intermediaries face mandatory compliance updates under revised FATCA/CRS rules within the Income-Tax Act 2025, tightened Domestic Money Transfer directions, and mandatory cyber resilience standards for non-bank payment operators.
